title: Volume 1 Prologue
content: Nearly half a century has passed since the invasion of monsters from another world began.
These monsters possessed similarities to the living creatures of Earth, but their ferocity and brutality were nothing alike.
Before long, these monsters came to be written as "False Beasts" and referred to as Gijuu, becoming the common enemy of all humanity.
When they were first discovered, the Gijuu were treated as monsters and demons.
For humanity at the time, who had not yet confirmed the existence of Gates, the Gijuu must have looked like monsters straight out of a work of fiction.
Appearing out of nowhere to antagonize humanity, the Gijuu were a severe threat.
In the early days, humanity was temporarily driven to the brink of extinction, but over decades, we managed to reach the point of destroying the Gates from which the Gijuu emerged.
Presently, dealing with the irregularly appearing Gates and the Gijuu that emerge from them has become humanity's war.
The shape of war has also changed.

In the past, nations reigned at the top and commanded wars, but now the Anti-Demon Elite Special Duty Agency—unofficially abbreviated as the "Fairy Agency"—stands in the position of unifying nations and issuing orders.
Today, wars between humans have drastically decreased, and the world is united in fighting against the Gijuu—or so the Fairy Agency officially announces.
Where the truth ends and the lies begin is impossible for a lowly soldier to know.
Yes, as a soldier, it is a matter I have no way of knowing, and at the same time, it has nothing to do with me.
After all, I am a weapon that goes by the name of a soldier.
Nowadays, powered suits are issued to each individual infantryman.

It is a weapon officially named the Special Reinforced Armor Suit. By equipping a rubber inner suit with artificial muscle functions, even ordinary people can output power surpassing that of a robust soldier.
The machine gun equipped on my right arm spews fire.
Even a machine gun with enough firepower to throw off a normal human and make aiming impossible can be handled with one hand if you have a powered suit.
Over the inner suit, we wear armor fitted with machinery and armaments.
This is the appearance of a modern infantryman.
The targets I point my muzzle at and scatter bullets toward are the Gijuu swarming out of a forest overgrown with eerie vegetation.
Class 3.
The Gijuu are classified by grade according to their threat level, with lower numbers being more dangerous.
Those Gijuu classified in the lowest rank mostly resembled insects or reptiles.
The most common type closely resembles Earth's ants, but their size is massive, ranging from two to three meters.
The Gijuu that appear from the other world through the Gates all possess ominous appearances.
What these monsters all have in common is a strong murderous intent toward humanity and Earth's flora and fauna.
Negotiations do not work on the Gijuu.
Appearing from suddenly spawned Gates, the Gijuu attacked humanity before any attempt at communication could be made.
While their overwhelming numbers were a threat even back then, the reason humanity was forced into a tough battle was due to the special forcefield possessed by the Gijuu.
When a machine gun bullet hits, a barrier-like object is generated on the surface of the Gijuu.
It can be pierced if it's only a Class 3 Gijuu, but it attenuates the power of the bullets.
Where it would normally take a few shots to destroy them, it takes dozens of hits to bring them down.
"...Reload."
I quickly swap the magazine and resume firing at the Gijuu.
To deal with them efficiently using a machine gun, it's best to concentrate hits on the same spot.
Weak points exist for each type of Gijuu, and aiming for them is also effective.
As I dispassionately dispatch the Gijuu while conserving ammunition, the Platoon Leader, wielding a large machine gun, shouts over the communicator.
"Looking sharp as always, Cherry! Keep gunning them down just like that!"
I give a short reply to the platoon leader's high-spirited words.
Cherry is something like a nickname for me.
Our platoon calls each other by nicknames.
"Sir, I'll do my best."
The military of the era before powered suits supposedly suffered considerable casualties against the Gijuu.
However, that doesn't mean we don't suffer casualties today.
"The neighboring platoon is getting chewed up!"
The male communications soldier, who acts as the platoon's hype man, is called MC by his comrades.
It supposedly means Master of Ceremonies, but he's a musician who dreams of reuniting with his bandmates and resuming his music career after he retires.
However, true to being a singer, his voice carries well.
Because he talks a lot, he also doubles as the platoon's mood-maker.
The platoon leader wore a bitter expression beneath his helmet.
"That's the 38th Platoon. Damn it, looking at them, they're going to have a hard time regrouping."
The helmet of the Special Reinforced Armor Suit has a monitor attached to the inside of the visor.
The AI inside the helmet displays the camera feed more clearly and easily.
Because there are cameras not only on the front but also on the back, you can check behind you like a car's rearview mirror.
A surrounding map is also displayed, making it obvious at a glance where your platoon members and allies are.
The faces of the members in the same platoon are also displayed small in the corner every time they speak over the comm line, showing fine attention to detail.
"Shy Boy! Can we provide cover?"
The one the platoon leader called out to was the platoon's marksman—not a sniper, but a soldier skilled at sharpshooting.
He was a quiet man, rarely speaking normally, which is why he was called Shy Boy.
"...It's possible. But the burden on our platoon will increase."
No one complains about Shy Boy mumbling.
It's because they know that's the kind of man he is, and there's no point in blaming him in this situation.
Above all, his sniping skills are recognized by everyone in the platoon.
A reliable man in the platoon, having heard Shy Boy's remark, advises the platoon leader.
His nickname is Gambler.
He's a man who boasts unparalleled strength in betting, and he has excellent intuition on the battlefield as well.
According to the platoon leader, the platoon has been saved many times by his judgment.
Excluding the platoon leader, he was the most reliable man in this platoon.
"If the neighbor collapses, the Gijuu will flood into our side too. Shy Boy alone isn't enough. Comic, Hairset, and I will go in to help."
Comic and Hairset, who were called out by Gambler, are Privates First Class who have just finished their training.
Comic was given the name for the simple reason that he aims to be a manga artist, and Hairset became known as Hairset because it takes him a long time to set his hair every morning.
"Are you sure it's okay for the two of us to leave!?"
"I don't want to get eaten while helping others!"
Even while complaining, both of them are fighting, and if ordered, they will probably go help the neighboring platoon.
Finally, a man known as Loser, the problem child of the platoon, calls out to the rookies.
"You idiots! We've got a man loved by the Goddess of Victory named Cherry right here. He says we can hold out even without you guys! Right, Cherry?"
Having the conversation thrown to me, I find myself at a loss for an answer.
"I never said I was loved by the Goddess of Victory though?"
"Cherry!! This is the scene where you say, 'Leave it to me!' and put the rookies at ease! What are you doing to my perfect pass!"
Loser is a cheerful and good-natured man even on the battlefield, but according to the platoon leader and Gambler, he's a happy-go-lucky problem child.
He's reliable on the battlefield, but unfortunately, his everyday life was the problem.
"...I apologize."
I ended up apologizing reflexively.
This man called Loser likes betting just as much as Gambler.
However, sadly, he's incredibly weak at it.
While Gambler is incredibly strong at betting, Loser just keeps losing when it comes to gambling and is always broke.
He keeps losing at gambling, hence Loser.
He has built up debts with various people, including me.
Hearing our exchange, Gambler exasperatedly tightens the reins on us.
"Cherry, you don't need to mind Loser's words. More importantly, you do your job. We believe in you."
Believe in me—I've bounced around several units up until now, but I've never had comrades say such words to me.
No, I only made comrades in the first place after coming to this platoon.
Before then, I was called a cyborg by those around me.
Calling me a cyborg wasn't entirely wrong.
I lost my parents when I was a child, and after that, I was picked up by a Fairy Agency facility.
It seemed the facility was running a project to turn children into military assets, and rigorous training was imposed on us almost daily.
As a result, without even attending school, I was raised in the facility to be a soldier solely for the purpose of killing Gijuu.
Having little emotion, dispassionately killing Gijuu according to orders—a cyborg created by the organization through modifications; that had been the surrounding perception of me until now.
"But I am—"
I was a test subject in a project to cultivate powerful infantrymen as a countermeasure against the Gijuu.
However, that project was judged to be ineffective and was canceled after massive numbers of infantrymen raised just like me died in combat.
We were a stain on the organization, and it seems we became a nuisance.
Even though we were essentially created for the organization, we were cast aside and lost our place.
One of the test subjects who died in combat had said it.
That we are pitiful weapons expected to die.
The platoon leader raises his voice at me as I hesitate.

"If you're going to grumble and complain, it's three hundred push-ups when we get back to base! Listen up, we don't care about your past. The only thing that matters is the fact that you, our comrade, are strong. Turn this situation around, Cherry!"
The gazes of the platoon members gather on me.
"Understood!"
Having exhausted the bullets in my machine gun, I decided to draw the attention of the Gijuu while Gambler and the others helped our allies.
Quickly changing the magazine, I break into a run, firing as I go.
Stopping my fire when I get close to the Gijuu, I hold a short sword in each hand.
The blade length is forty centimeters.
Because a knife lacks the reliable length to pierce the Gijuu's armor and deal a fatal wound, these are close-combat weapons prepared for infantry.
Holding one in each hand, I slash at the attacking Gijuu while dodging their strikes.
Kicking off the ground and leaping up, I land on the head of an ant-type Gijuu approaching with its large mandibles clacking, and forcefully stab the thin joint connecting to its torso.
For an instant, I felt slight resistance.
The forcefield must have rejected the blade of the short sword, but I forcefully thrust it in and break through.
The strike, powered not just by artificial muscles but also by my own trained muscular strength, was seemingly too much for the Gijuu to endure.
Its head was severed from its torso, scattering bodily fluids.
Perhaps angered that their comrade was killed, or perhaps just harboring murderous intent to attack because I am human, the insect-type Gijuu begin crying out, making an unpleasant grinding noise.
Tripping over each other to attack, they do not appear to be considering any tactics.
They probably aren't actually thinking, but humanity continues to suffer from the offensives utilizing the sheer numbers of the Gijuu.
While dodging the Gijuu's attacks, I slash away with the short swords gripped in both hands.
There are individuals that carelessly approach and expose their weak points, and in those cases, it's the machine gun's turn.
As the muzzle spits fire, I deliver a bullet directly into the open mouth of a Gijuu.
The figure of the Gijuu bursting open from the inside is quickly trampled by the Gijuu coming from behind and disappears from sight.
In a situation completely surrounded by enemies, I keep moving and taking down the Gijuu.
Just as I was taught at the facility—killing my heart—and merely executing my mission as a weapon to defeat the Gijuu.
It's likely the result of the training I underwent to kill my emotions.
We have an extremely thin sense of fear.
We possess a survival instinct, but compared to ordinary people, it must be quite dull.
Because we were adjusted that way.
While focusing on defeating the enemies in front of me, I notice that before I knew it, many Gijuu corpses are scattered around me.
A Gijuu closing in on me gets its head blown off by Shy Boy's sniping, bringing me back to my senses.
"That's enough, come back... Cherry."
For some reason, Shy Boy gets embarrassed only when calling my name, but it seems I'm done buying time.
As I regroup with my comrades while being covered, the platoon leader shouts to everyone.
"Get down!"
As everyone hits the deck in unison, artillery fire rains down on the massive swarm of surging Gijuu.
The sound of explosions and tremors echo deep into our bodies, and the shockwaves shake us.
Perhaps the Gijuu carried seeds, but the blasts swallowed up and blew away the gradually expanding, unearthly vegetation.
When the bombardment ceases, MC is the first to raise his head.
"Whoa, blew 'em away beautifully. The artillery corps is the best. But if they could do this much, I wish they'd just blown them away from the start."
The platoon leader retorts with his usual scolding to the complaining MC.
"They could execute it because we bought time and held them at this spot. ...Hm? Looks like the Goddesses are making an appearance too."
The platoon leader was looking at the sky as he spoke.
Prompted, I also look up to see three contrails.
Checking with the maximum telephoto of the camera built into my helmet, entities with the figures of women were flying in the sky.
"...Valkyries."
They are the star attractions of the modern battlefield, and humanity's trump card capable of taking on Gijuu Class 2 and above.
They are clad in armor named Valkyrie, but the armor is only equipped on their arms and legs.
Much like the Gijuu, a special forcefield apparently protects them, making it unnecessary to cover themselves in armor.
Some apparently voice concern about whether they're scared being exposed like that, but the ones they fight are all larger and stronger than the Gijuu we face on the ground.
It's said that if we infantrymen encounter a Class 2 or higher and survive, it's a miracle.
Those very Class 2s are treated as small fry by them, the Valkyries.
For the Fairy Agency, the vital military asset isn't us on the ground, but them dancing in the sky.
After all, only they can handle the Valkyrie Dresses.
Not only do they not react to men, but even if they could be moved, it supposedly wouldn't mean anything.
The men of the modern era could only fight grubbily on the ground like us.
As I gaze in fascination, the platoon leader throws a chuckle.
"You really love the Goddesses, huh. Even if you stare that hard, they ain't gonna look our way."
Called out, I remember where I am.
This is a battlefield, and looking up at the sky defenselessly is out of the question.
"Tch! My deepest apologies!"
"Be careful. And once we finish off the surviving Gijuu, we're pulling out. Let's wrap this up quick and head back to base."
"Sir!"
The platoon leader smiled with a troubled look at me as I straightened my spine and saluted.
"You really are stiff, aren't you."
Once the battle is over and it's time to return to base, we climb into the bed of an arriving truck.
Other platoons also ride in the same truck bed, but many have lost comrades and their numbers have dwindled.
Breaking the depressed atmosphere in the truck bed is Comic.
Taking off his helmet, he pulls out a notepad and starts jotting down material of some sort.
He often said he was gathering material now so he could make it as a manga artist once he retired.
Talking to me sitting next to him must be part of that.
"Corporal, the battle today was amazing. Is there a secret to your strength or something?"
It would be fine if I could answer honestly, but the project that raised me binds me to a confidentiality agreement, even if it's been canceled.
Many know the story, but it's not something I can speak of, as it's not the kind of information they prefer to spread.
"I just diligently digest my training."
"Is that really it?"
When a topic interests him, Comic is persistent.
Ignoring him and letting it pass is an option, but it's annoying how he'll keep talking until he gives up.
"Face forward and advance step by step... The secret is the accumulation of each day."
"Wasn't that your favorite family motto, Corporal?"
"Yeah, heard it from my mother. Apparently it's my grandmother's words."
Face forward and advance step by step, don't look around, securely move forward on your own two feet—that's the teaching.
It's not quite enough to be called a family motto, but they are words that have supported me this far.

"Steady effort, huh? For that, your strength is extraordinary. The way you fight holding short swords, you were like a ninja. Oh, want to switch to a katana next time? I think dual-wielding them would look great."
I tilt my head in confusion.

"We infantry don't have katanas in our equipment, though? Besides, having a blade longer than this makes it inconvenient to carry. In the first place, avoiding close-quarters combat as much as possible is basic—"
"Ah, yes. Um, that's enough."
Thinking the conversation would drag on, Comic cut off his interview with me.
When the conversation breaks, Hairset speaks to me next.

"Come to think of it, there was a story I was curious about too. You and your squad recovered a fallen Valkyrie before, right, Corporal? Did anything happen then? You know, like a battlefield romance or something."
The rookies all call me by my rank, but they've opened up to me a lot more than before.
For their sake, I try to recall the story of the fallen Valkyrie, but there was nothing like what they were hoping for.
To begin with, the Valkyries who fall and are recovered by ground forces are generally in a foul mood.
Recovering Valkyries who fall to the ground due to being shot down or accidents is our job.
We are expected to jump into any dangerous situation and recover them at the risk of our lives.
The lives of the Valkyries take utmost priority over ours—that is the current battlefield.
"I barely spoke with her when we recovered her. We just delivered her to the destination and handed her over to another unit."
Perhaps dreaming of the battlefield, the two looked bored by my answer.
Hairset is disappointed, and Comic looks regretful.
"No battlefield romance, huh."
"I thought a romance between a Valkyrie and an infantryman would make for good material though."
Gambler, who had been listening to our silly conversation, steps in to teach the two reality on my behalf.
"Do you guys not know what the Valkyries call us infantry? Apparently they call us crawling around on the ground in our black suits 'ants'."
Hearing Gambler's story, the two had surprised looks on their faces.
They must have been shocked to learn they were called the same thing as the Gijuu they were desperately fighting just moments ago.
Even Loser joins in this conversation.

"Even after we risk danger to recover them, it's just 'Too slow!' without a word of thanks, right? It makes you sick when we put our lives on the line. The folks up in heaven are too stuck up for their own good."
Loser laughed, shaking his head side to side as he recalled that time.
However, it seemed our atmosphere was intolerable to those around us.
The gazes of the other platoon members riding with us gathered on us.
"You guys have been yapping and acting all bubbly for a while now. You're not women or children, can't you keep it quiet?"
Their equipment was damaged, and blood was seeping from the bandages wrapped around several of them.
It seemed they had lost comrades as well.
One of the men looks at me and distorts his face in displeasure.
"You're that cyborg survivor? Creepy."
When I, called a cyborg, advert my gaze, the opponent raises his voice as if venting his frustration.
"You seem to have plenty of leeway. I guess this level of a battlefield doesn't even serve as a warm-up for Mr. Slaughter Weapon? I'm so jealous."
I've faced unreasonable false accusations like this frequently in the past.
They too have faced unreasonable situations on the battlefield and must be mentally cornered.
Besides, while I wouldn't go so far as slaughter weapon, it's a fact that I received special training and was enhanced.
As I remained silent without arguing back, the platoon leader, arms crossed, glared at the opponent.
"Do you have some business with my subordinate? I'll hear you out."
When the platoon leader glared, the opponent turned his face away, perhaps sensing he was at a disadvantage.
MC calls out to me.
"Don't worry about it. They're just hurting from losing their buddies."
"I'm fine."
I've faced an environment where people take their anger out on me.
My special position probably looks creepy to those around me.
But even I managed to make comrades.
Shy Boy offers me a mint-flavored combat ration.
The square, stick-shaped thing wrapped in silver foil is distributed to infantry when they sortie.
"Eat."
"...Thank you very much. I accept."
Mint flavor is Shy Boy's favorite, but him handing it over to me means he's probably showing concern.
I've belonged to several platoons, but I felt a sense of comfort in my current one.
Just as I was about to bite into the mint-flavored combat ration, the truck carrying us slammed on the brakes.
As we in the truck bed fell sideways, an infantryman from another platoon yelled toward the driver's seat.
"That hurt!"
We agreed with his sentiment, but an explosion went off nearby.
I immediately put on my helmet and entered a combat stance.
The platoon follows me into a combat stance, but the sounds of explosions can be heard one after another from our surroundings.
The platoon leader grabs his weapon and jumps outside.
"What the hell is happening? Our status check must be fast!"
Stepping outside and checking the surroundings, the trucks that had been transporting us infantry were being destroyed one after another.
Wondering what was going on, there was a three-meter-tall humanoid Gijuu in our path of travel.
Emitting the ominous appearance and presence typical of a Gijuu, I had never seen that thing before.
I'd never even heard of a humanoid type existing in the first place.
Two horns extending from its head.
That slender and tall figure.
It had something like wings on its back, and it was spreading and moving them.
It also has a tail, but seeing that thing fully worthy of being called humanoid—MC runs a match.
"Unknown? It's an unconfirmed entity!"
When there is no information on the enemy at all, we have to move under the assumption it's Class 2 or higher.
Us infantry can't possibly take on an opponent Class 2 or higher; we would merely be trampled.
We should have hurried to retreat from this place, but—
"Wha!?"
By the time I noticed, MC's upper half had been blown away.
His lower half slowly collapses.
Before anyone knew it, the humanoid Gijuu was standing right beside MC.
What happened? When did it move? Why MC? Even confused, having been trained, I had instantly pulled the trigger of my machine gun.
"I'll handle this one!"
It was an action meant to let the platoon comrades escape in the meantime, but the machine gun bullets were repelled by the forcefield generated by the humanoid Gijuu and dealt no damage.
The humanoid Gijuu had two red lines like tears flowing from its almond-shaped eyes—its mouth looked like it was smiling.
In the next moment, I was blown away and rolling on the ground.
I didn't even have time to break my fall.
Unable to fully process what happened, I hear the voices of my comrades.
"How dare you do that to Cherry!"
The platoon leader's machine gun spits fire, but soon stops making noise.
Gambler screams.
"Comic, Hairset, at least you guys—"
Gambler's voice disappeared as well.
I desperately try to stand up, but it seems my leg is broken.
Unable to stand properly, I vomited blood inside my helmet.
My internal organs took damage too.
"You bastard, for Gambler!"
I heard Loser's voice—or so I thought, but it disappeared immediately.
Stop. Please don't fight, run away.
I wanted to scream, but no voice came out.
"Uwaaaaah!!"
"Stay awayyyyy!!"
I heard the sound of Comic and Hairset firing, but that sound also stopped right away.
Around me, other platoons were showing their backs to the humanoid Gijuu and running away, screaming, but they were shot from behind and collapsed one after another.
By the time I somehow managed to stand up, the humanoid Gijuu had grabbed Shy Boy and lifted him up.
"Shy Boy!"
Before I could finish calling his name, Shy Boy pointed his rifle at the humanoid Gijuu and pulled the trigger repeatedly.
He looks at me and says,
"Run... away."
The moment he finished speaking, Shy Boy was crushed in the grip of the humanoid Gijuu.
The humanoid Gijuu licks its hand stained red.
Before I knew it, the surrounding allies were gone, and silence spread.
The comrades I was having conversations with just moments ago were scattered around as mangled corpses.
My breathing becomes erratic.
I can't fully accept the reality before my eyes.
Even with my dulled instincts, it was completely obvious that the Gijuu in front of me was an existence I couldn't defeat.
Even so, I raise my right arm and point the muzzle of my machine gun at the humanoid Gijuu.
Dragging my leg as if to step forward, I grip a short sword in my left hand.
"You... are the only one I'll—!"

What meaning is there in this action? Am I not just provoking the enemy? If I stay quiet, isn't there a chance I'll be overlooked? Thoughts of such possibilities crossed my mind, but for some reason, I ignored them all and directed my murderous intent at the humanoid Gijuu.
The enemy—looked like it was smiling.
When its fingertip pointed toward me, my right arm was pierced by a light and burned away.
If I try to run with a broken leg, my left leg is pierced by a light fired from the humanoid Gijuu's fingertip.
Is it toying with me for fun? The humanoid Gijuu's actions made me grit my back teeth in frustration.
Falling forward, I am now entirely at the mercy of the enemy.
I was prepared to die on the battlefield eventually.
But, when I was actually about to meet my death—I never thought my heart would feel this unsettled.
The monitor inside the helmet is cracked, the AI isn't functioning, and the image is in black and white with terrible noise.
Wanting to at least burn the enemy's figure into my eyes, I look up, only to see something fluttering down from the sky.
"Valky...rie."
Swooping down to wedge herself between me and the humanoid Gijuu was a Valkyrie, who should have been indifferent to ground battles.
Could she not ignore the irregularity of a humanoid type and swooped down?
Appearing completely alone, the Valkyrie has her back turned and I can't see her face.
The image noise is terrible, and I can't catch the picked-up transmission well either.
"Too fast—Suddenly—"
[img]https://i.imgur.com/RfpTAgy.jpeg
"Like hell I'll let you—!"
The Valkyrie challenged the Gijuu that we couldn't even put a dent in.
While looking at her back, I lost consciousness.
When I woke up, I was in a place that looked like a hospital.
The reason I'm vague and say 'looked like' is because only my bed was prepared in a large room.
Looking around, there was an exorbitant amount of medical equipment lined up, and even life support systems were prepared.
Looking at my own body, my heart must have failed too.
Right now, a machine was acting as my heart in its stead.
My field of vision is also narrow. It seems I took an injury to my left eye as well.
Seeing myself receiving such generous medical treatment, I felt a sense of incongruity even though it was happening to me.
Because there is no reason to go this far for a mere infantryman.
To the Fairy Agency—the organization—I am an existence they want to disappear as soon as possible.
There's no reason to spend money to keep me alive.
As I lay in bed pondering the reason for this unnatural situation, the door to the room opened.
"Hey, I heard you woke up so I came flying over. Nice to meet you, Corporal Hifumi Ren."
The person looked like an elderly man, but his speech and conduct were like a child's.
Since he's wearing a lab coat, is he a doctor?
The small, slightly-built man wearing glasses had small eyes, but his pupils sparkled brightly.
He presses the tablet terminal he held in both hands toward me lying there, as if to show it off.
"I know it's sudden, but won't you volunteer for an experiment? I've been waiting for an existence like you all this time."
With his sudden appearance and abrupt proposal, I demand an explanation.
"Even if you say experiment, I'm in this kind of physical state. Moreover, I'm hated by the organization."
"You're a surviving enhanced soldier, right? Of course, I've gotten permission. When I negotiated with the higher-ups saying survivors like you guys are optimal, they agreed to it."
He asks me to participate in the experiment while knowing my past.
It seems the severity of my injuries doesn't matter either.
"May I ask the details of the experiment?"
"I don't mind, but if you hear it, there's no turning back."
"Even if I refuse, I'll just die like this anyway."
It seems the reason my life is being sustained is because the man before me requested my participation in the experiment. If I refuse here, they'll just turn off the life support and I'll die anyway.
The man explains the project while his glasses gleam suspiciously.
"The Prometheus Project... It was given a grandiose name, but in short, it's about trying to birth a hero."
"A hero?"
"Yes. A hero. Boys love them, don't they? I love them too."
The man is acting excitedly like a child.

"Currently, the only ones who can counter the Gijuu are limited to the Valkyries. However, the battle dresses operated by the Valkyries have a flaw in that they can only be handled by women. No matter what men did, they couldn't handle them, but if that's the case, we just need to complete an anti-Gijuu weapon that men can handle."
Talks of this kind have come up many times, but I've heard they all ended in failure.
To begin with, the powered suits we used were originally developed for anti-Gijuu use too.
Though there was no chance of winning against a Class 2 or higher enemy.
"I've heard that militarizing men has been planned many times before and failed."
"Ah, that's right. Because the approach was wrong from the start."
The man operates his tablet terminal, switches the screen, and shows me top-secret data.
"The forcefield the Gijuu use is magic? Is this some kind of joke?"
"The higher-ups just call that special forcefield that. However, it's not only the Gijuu who can manipulate this power. It's the same for the Valkyries too."
The Valkyries are the same? They could counter them because they could wield the same power?
The man makes his proposal to me.
"We'll perform regenerative treatment on your lost limbs and organs. However—the cells we use will be harvested from a Gijuu."
"That's—!"
When I raised my voice, a severe pain ran through my body.
As my face contorts in agony, the man nods several times.

"If the goal is to be able to use the same magic as the Gijuu, we just need to regenerate limbs from Gijuu cells and make them usable. We somehow managed to find a method for that and acquired the best cells... but a problem occurred here."
The man continues with a troubled face.

"There are no volunteers willing to accept the surgery. Even when there were, every single one of them broke, unable to withstand the intense pain accompanying the surgery and rehabilitation. But you guys are different. Your emotions are suppressed, and you've been enhanced to endure severe pain, haven't you?"
Having Gijuu cells embedded in your own body, and what waits after is excruciating pain.
With that, gathering test subjects would be extremely difficult.
There's no doubt that dying just like this would be a far more peaceful death.
Even so, I couldn't help but ask.
"May I ask what the success rate is?"
"Less than ten percent."
The man replied without a hint of remorse.
Is that his attempt at sincerity? In the first place, he doesn't look like he even considers I would decline this offer.
The man seems to merely want to prove that his own theories are correct.

"Of course, I promise my utmost effort. I'll make sure to raise the success rate even a little, and if successful, you'll be a pilot. Because it wouldn't look good for you to remain a Corporal, it's been arranged to prepare the rank of Warrant Officer for you. A major promotion."
The humanoid weapon that suffered a helpless defeat against a Class 2 should have had its development canceled a long time ago.
I felt a sense of affinity with the pitiful circumstance—where the project was canceled and then repurposed—just like me.
"—I volunteer."
When I say I will undergo the surgery, the man brings the tablet terminal right under my nose.
"Then please sign right away! Ah, I'm late in giving my name. My name is John Smith. I received a new name from the organization."
John Smith—it seems that's not his real name.
When I signed with my trembling left hand, the man happily left the room.
"I'll go prepare for the surgery right away!"
From that attitude, he'll probably return very shortly.
While thinking I did something foolish, I look at my left hand and clench it.
"It's my life with no use anyway. If so, using it for a project that has even a little meaning isn't bad."
We were raised to be of use to the organization.
Even now, that purpose hasn't changed.
And yet, for some reason, the faces of my dead comrades came to mind.
